cards.b: The net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration (down a concentration gradient), as a result of their random movement.
Passive: no energy from respiration is needed.

cards.f: Four factors that increase the rate of diffusion
cards.b: Larger surface area, higher temperature, steeper concentration gradient, shorter distance.
Net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential (dilute solution) to lower water potential (concentrated solution) through a partially permeable membrane.

cards.f: Which solution has the highest water potential?
cards.b: Pure water. The more solute dissolved, the lower the water potential.
Movement of particles through a cell membrane from lower to higher concentration (against the gradient) using energy from respiration.

cards.f: Why do root hair cells use active transport?
cards.b: To take up ions such as nitrate and magnesium that are at a lower concentration in soil water than in the cell.
A plant cell swollen with water, its contents pushing against the cell wall (turgor pressure). The wall stops it bursting.
The cell membrane and cytoplasm pull away from the cell wall as the cell loses water by osmosis.

cards.f: What happens to a red blood cell in pure water?
cards.b: Water enters by osmosis; the cell swells and bursts because it has no cell wall.

cards.f: Elements in carbohydrates, proteins and fats
cards.b: Carbohydrates and fats: C, H, O. Proteins: C, H, O, N (some also S).

cards.f: What are these large molecules made from: starch, protein, fats?
cards.b: Starch: glucose. Protein: amino acids. Fats and oils: fatty acids and glycerol.

cards.f: Iodine test and Benedict's test results
cards.b: Iodine: starch turns blue-black. Benedict's (heat in water bath): reducing sugar goes green → yellow → orange → brick-red; stays blue if absent.

cards.f: Biuret test and ethanol emulsion test results
cards.b: Biuret: protein turns purple/violet (stays blue if absent). Ethanol emulsion: fats/oils give a cloudy white emulsion.

cards.f: Formula for percentage change in mass
cards.b: (final mass − initial mass) ÷ initial mass × 100. Use this because cylinders start with different masses.

short.q: Explain why the rate of diffusion is faster at a higher temperature. [2]
short.model: At higher temperature particles have more kinetic energy and move faster, so there is a greater net movement down the concentration gradient.
points: particles have more kinetic energy / move faster
so more net movement / diffusion is quicker

short.q: Potato cylinders are placed in concentrated sucrose solution and lose mass. Explain why. [3]
short.model: The solution has a lower water potential than the potato cells, so water leaves the cells by osmosis through the partially permeable membrane.
points: solution has lower water potential than cells

short.q: A potato cylinder of 2.80 g becomes 2.52 g. Calculate the percentage change in mass. [2]
Explain how a root hair cell takes up nitrate ions from soil with a lower nitrate concentration than the cell. [3]
short.model: By active transport against the concentration gradient, using energy from respiration in mitochondria.

short.q: Describe how to test a food for protein and state the positive result. [2]
short.model: Add biuret reagent to the food sample; it turns purple/violet if protein is present.
points: add biuret reagent (or NaOH then copper sulfate)
